messages:
ana: Quick follow-up on the dedicated pool autoscale surface. sketching a few concrete interface scenarios we should validate before the RFC. want quick eyes.

mike: ack. can you list the scenarios? would love to see failure modes too.

ana: first scenario: operator -> runtime prewarm request with hard headroom. operator asks pool to ensure N slots pinned for tenant for the next T minutes. runtime may decline if fragmentation prevents satisfying request. expected response states: accepted | deferred | rejected, plus best-effort prewarm ETA.

jin: +1. question: do we allow runtime to return partial acceptance (eg 3/5 slots) or only binary? partial seems useful but complicates billing.

ana: leaning partial acceptance. operator should be able to accept partial and hold a soft reservation for remainder. include reservation_id for later idempotent top-ups.

luca: scenario two: admission-time QoS hint. tenant sends {qos: latency | throughput, target_p99_ms, cost_budget}. runtime must pick a plan: DIRECT_DEDICATED, ACCEPTED_BURST, QUEUED_WITH_BACKOFF, or REJECTED_COST.

sarah: for QUEUED_WITH_BACKOFF, should runtime stream ETA updates to the operator or should control plane poll?

ana: prefer streaming ETA via control-plane websocket for UX. include pull fallback. updates frequency small (eg every 5s).

jin: failure mode: operator asks prewarm, runtime accepts but GPU init fails (driver OOM, MIG misconfig). runtime should mark reservation FAILED with failure_reason; operator gets webhook + suggested fallback (burst lane or hosted).

luca: also add a prewarm-health probe: runtime runs lightweight model load check and marks slot READY only if probe passes.

ana: proposed minimal API shape (pseudo as a string payload): { admit_request_id, tenant_id, requested_capacity_units, prewarm, headroom_minutes, qos, target_p99_ms, cost_budget_usd_hour, allow_partial }. we'll spec this in protobuf in the RFC.

mike: nit: `requested_capacity_units` maps better to fractional-slab models. +1 on `allow_partial` field.

orch-bot: operator-event: reservation_created id=rez-6500 tenant=acme stacks=3 prewarm=true

jin: telemetry: we need decision rationale for why runtime chose ACCEPTED_BURST vs DIRECT_DEDICATED to debug cost/latency regressions. include `decision_reason` and `score_vector` in accept responses.

luca: oscillation safety: runtime must apply hysteresis (eg 30s) before deallocating recently-provisioned slots unless explicit operator drain requested. add `min_lifetime_seconds` on reservations.

sarah: test plan sketched: 1) synthetic spike test to validate admission path + ETA accuracy; 2) inject driver OOM during prewarm; 3) partial-acceptance billing reconciliation test; 4) churn test measuring oscillation under noisy traffic.

ana: final ask: thumbs-up to include these scenarios in the RFC follow-up and spec protobuf + control-plane events? i'll draft the follow-up PR with proto + sample telemetry.

mike: +1.

jin: +1. add small example webhook payload for failure in PR.

luca: +1. ensure operator API backward compatibility section in the doc.

sarah: +1. i'll add the synthetic load harness to the autoscale sim.

ana: thanks all 44d i'll open the follow-up RFC this afternoon and ping reviewers.
